beats.text: A radio telescope in Ohio picked up a signal nobody saw arrive.
beats.note: Big Ear's computer printed it at about 11:16 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time. No one was at the telescope at that time. Jerry Ehman found it a few days later.
Ehman circled the characters 6EQUJ5 on the printout and wrote 'Wow!' beside them.

beats.text: Each character is a signal strength.
beats.note: One character per 12 second row of printout. The values climbed through 6, E and Q to U, then fell to J and 5. U stood for 30, the largest value seen.

beats.context: The longest Big Ear could watch one patch of sky as the Earth turned. The signal lasted the whole window.

beats.text: It sat just above the hydrogen line.
beats.note: Ehman's figure is 1420.4556 megahertz, about 50 kilohertz above the hydrogen line, in a single narrow channel.
Ehman searched in the months afterwards, and later searches, including the Very Large Array, found nothing. No explanation is settled.

beats.text: The most famous signal in the search for aliens is one pen mark on one printout.

beats.line: Write 'Wow' next to the weird data.
